gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on BLUETTI's US store today the 1,152 Wh AC180 is in stock at $499, the same price as the 1,024 Wh Elite 100 V2 ChatGPT showed, and that a non-WiFIRE Traeger at its stated 0.4–0.8 A after heat-up uses about 576–1,152 Wh in 12 hours, which can exceed what any of ChatGPT's ~1 kWh cards hold, while the 2,073.6 Wh Elite 200 V2 at $899 covers it.
standout_why: I compared against Traeger Support (cited in all three chats; it gives per-model watts and post-heating amps but no watt-hours per cook and no stations), Volt & Valley (prices four stations, but the AC180 and the 2 kWh class aren't among them, and its runtimes assume a flat 50 W, which isn't measured) and ChatGPT's own cards ($449.99 C1000 at Micro Center, $499 Elite 100 V2, $509 Jackery from Eco Solar Kits, $729 AC180 from an unnamed seller). None prices the AC180 at BLUETTI's $499, none puts price per Wh side by side, and none turns Traeger's amp figures into a 12-hour watt-hour total. That total is what rules out 1 kWh units for older Traegers. I could not open the cited Pit Boss manual's text (compressed PDF), so I can't compare against its 1,000 W inverter claim.
decides: At $499 the AC180 beats the Elite 100 V2 on capacity at the same price, and it beats ChatGPT's $729 AC180 card by $230, so it should be the 1 kWh-class pick. Our page's AC180 stock cell ('Back late Nov') is out of date: it is in stock today. If the shopper's grill is a non-WiFIRE Traeger (300 W rated, 0.4–0.8 A after heat-up), the 12-hour total can pass 1 kWh, so the Elite 200 V2 at $899 (2,073.6 Wh) becomes the safe pick. A Traeger D2 (0.08–0.17 A, about 10–20 W) needs only about 115–245 Wh at the plug, so a 1 kWh unit gives several nights and even the 288 Wh Elite 30 V2 at $289.99 is borderline. The ALLPOWERS P1800 is the cheapest per Wh ($399 for 1,024 Wh), but I couldn't open its product page to resolve whether it ships now or is a pre-order.

findings.label: Traeger non-WiFIRE grill draw
findings.value: 300 W / 2.5 A rated at 120 V; drops to 0.4–0.8 A after heating
findings.source_title: Grill Watt & Amp Usage – Traeger Support
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.4–0.8 A × 120 V = 48–96 W; × 12 h = 576–1,152 Wh at the plug, before inverter loss and igniter start. The top of that range is more than the 1,024–1,070 Wh rated capacity of every ~1 kWh card ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Traeger D2 grill draw
findings.value: 110 W / 0.9 A rated at 120 V; drops to 0.08–0.17 A after heating
findings.source_title: Grill Watt & Amp Usage – Traeger Support
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.08–0.17 A × 120 V ≈ 10–20 W; × 12 h ≈ 115–245 Wh at the plug. The page also lists Woodridge at 535 W and Touchscreen (grill only) at 95 W, with no post-heating figure for either.
